correctness.rationale: The signed Green cap identity differentiates exactly to 2B'(s)=[q-p,u+v] and B''(s)=-[u,v] on every fixed edge-pair interval. Convexity forbids equal directed edge tangents; thus only opposed parallel tangents create constant cap areas. Finitely many nonconstant quadratic branches yield only absolutely continuous inverse-square-root densities. For a proper trapezoid the strict reverse triangle inequality guarantees exactly one overlap interval of length shorter base on each half-perimeter, and direct shoelace/trapezoid area gives z*=1/2-|c-d|/(2(a+b)); the probability is 2min(a,b)/P. All edge/limiting parallelogram cases are handled. The standalone checker completed 948 exact/geometric assertions. Finite numerical work does not replace the continuum proof.

value.rationale: The statistic arises naturally when cutting a convex boundary at two arclength-antipodal endpoints, a standard geometric bisection construction. The theorem gives a complete measure-type classification for all convex polygons and a sharp atomic inverse diagnostic for all convex quadrilaterals. An atom detects trapezoid parallelism, its probability encodes a genuinely geometric side length and its location detects unequal legs, while the complement has an explicit inverse-square-root density structure. These facts are not merely a rephrasing of Harned's envelope classification; they quantify an independent area observable across an entire natural shape family. No broader reconstruction or downstream result is claimed.
